title: Tor-amplitude gap forces derived tensor cohomology to vanish
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let P be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] with Tor amplitude in [u,v], meaning that H^i(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)=0 for every \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G and every i\notin[u,v], and let L be a complex with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category]. For every integer j, if H^q(L)=0 for all q in [j-v,j-u], then H^j(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}L)=0.

source.place: Tag 09M4, proof, spectral sequence after the sentence 'Say K^\vee has tor amplitude in [a,b]'

proof.text: Let U be an affine open of X on which P|_U is isomorphic in D(\mathcal O_U) to a strictly perfect complex Q^\bullet [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Each Q^p is a direct summand of a finite free \mathcal O_U-module, hence flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] (elementary), and Q^\bullet is bounded, so Q^\bullet is K-flat [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Derived tensor product commutes with restriction to the open U, and restriction preserves K-flatness (elementary: for an acyclic complex \mathcal F^\bullet on U the extension by zero j_!\mathcal F^\bullet is acyclic and \mathrm{Tot}(j_!\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes K^\bullet)|_U=\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes K^\bullet|_U)). Hence for every complex M of \mathcal O_X-modules, (P\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)|_U is represented by the total tensor complex \mathrm{Tot}(Q^\bullet\otimes M|_U) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In particular (P\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)|_U\cong\mathrm{Tot}(Q^\bullet\otimes L|_U), and, applying the Tor-amplitude hypothesis to the \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G=H^q(L), H^p(Q^\bullet\otimes H^q(L)|_U)=0 for every q and every p\notin[u,v].

source.place: Tag 09M4, proof, spectral sequence after the sentence 'Say K^\vee has tor amplitude in [a,b]'

proof.text: Filter K^\bullet=\mathrm{Tot}(Q^\bullet\otimes L|_U) by Q-degree: F^pK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}Q^i\otimes L^{n-i}|_U. These are subcomplexes, and the filtration is bounded because Q^\bullet is bounded; \mathrm{gr}^pK^\bullet=Q^p\otimes L|_U[-p]. The bounded filtered-complex spectral sequence [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] has E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\mathrm{gr}^pK^\bullet)=H^q(Q^p\otimes L|_U)=Q^p\otimes H^q(L)|_U, the last equality because Q^p is flat so Q^p\otimes- is exact (elementary). The differential d_1, the connecting map of 0\to\mathrm{gr}^{p+1}\to F^p/F^{p+2}\to\mathrm{gr}^p\to0, is induced by the differential of Q^\bullet, so E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Q^\bullet\otimes H^q(L)|_U), which vanishes for p\notin[u,v] by Step 1. Now assume H^q(L)=0 for every q in [j-v,j-u]. For p+q=j, either p\notin[u,v] and E_2^{p,q}=0, or p\in[u,v], so q=j-p\in[j-v,j-u] and already E_1^{p,q}=0. Later pages are subquotients, so E_\infty^{p,j-p}=0 for all p, and by the convergence clause of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] all graded pieces of the finite filtration on H^j(K^\bullet) vanish.

source.place: Tag 09M4, proof, spectral sequence vanishing in the Tor-amplitude gap

proof.text: A finite filtration whose associated graded objects are all zero is zero, so H^j((P\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}L)|_U)=H^j(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}L)|_U=0. Such affine opens U cover X and vanishing of a sheaf is local, so H^j(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}L)=0.
